annotations.annotation_text: Viconian philosophical framework: Giambattista Vico's cyclical schema of history (divine theocratic age, heroic aristocratic age, human democratic age, and ricorso), invoked through "heroic".
sources: Vico, Giambattista. Scienza Nuova (The New Science, 1725). https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/vico/
Beckett, Samuel, et al. Our Exagmination Round His Factification... https://archive.org/details/ourexagminationr0000unse
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Giambattista Vico. https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/vico/

annotations.annotation_text: Universal archetype of the father and everyman protagonist Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker (HCE), manifested here as "porter". Represents the recumbent Dublin landscape with head at Howth and body stretching west to Phoenix Park.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: The nocturnal oneiric dimension (Night): Joyce's exploration of the sleeping body, sensory deprivation, auditory distortions, and the somatic language of the collective unconscious.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349

annotations.annotation_text: The Book of Kells manuscript tradition (Tunc page): Joyce equates the text of Finnegans Wake and the Hen's letter to the labyrinthine Celtic interlacing and enigmatic Latin glosses of the 8th-century Gospel book.
sources: Trinity College Dublin: The Book of Kells Online. https://digitalcollections.tcd.ie/concern/works/hm50tr726
Sullivan, Sir Edward. The Book of Kells. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/16436
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Ancient Egyptian eschatology (set): HCE as the dismembered and resurrected god Osiris, ALP as Isis gathering his scattered limbs, and the dream journey through the underworld (Tuat).
sources: Budge, E.A. Wallis. The Book of the Dead (The Papyrus of Ani). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1300
Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark (The Egyptian Wake). https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish

annotations.annotation_text: The Four Old Men (Mamalujo: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; Ulster, Munster, Leinster, Connaught; the Four Annalists of Ireland), chronicling the cycles of human history as judges, senile bed-sitters, and circling seagulls.
sources: O'Donovan, John. The Annals of the Four Masters. https://celt.ucc.ie/published/T100005A/
The Four Gospels (King James Bible). https://www.biblegateway.com
MacCabe, Colin. James Joyce and the Revolution of the Word. https://archive.org/details/jamesjoycerevolu0000macc
